defect_observations: C005: Durrett states Theorem 1.1.1 (ii) for a cover A contained in the union of the A_m and names it subadditivity; the routed item 2 gives the union form without the name. The covering form follows in one line from items 1 and 2 of the same theorem, so the component is judged covered; the unrouted owned lemma (owned body lines 253-312) states it with the name and an example.

C015: Durrett's Theorem 1.3.5 (f Borel measurable from R^n to R) is not written as a separate sentence; it is the composite rule applied to the measurable vector map, both stated in the entry (lines 292-294), and was judged covered.
C003: Durrett's Example 1.1.6 uses the integers; the routed example uses the positive integers with the same argument. The unrouted owned text (owned body lines 246-250) records the integer form.

C025: the boundary cites Durrett for the measure existence argument but does not cross-reference the handbook's own construction in the next routed chapter (measure-extension.tex: thm:p15-lebesgue-unit-interval line 216, thm:p15-cdf-existence line 287). A cross-reference would remove the reader's dependence on the source citation.
Chapter opening (lines 11-14) attributes the chapter's development to secs. 1.1-1.3 and app. A.1, while the app. A.1 construction is deferred by the closing boundary (lines 458-470).

Lines 348-352 warn that limiting upper and lower values may both be infinite, which answers Durrett's description limsup X_n - liminf X_n = 0 of Omega_o (p. 16), but the source formula is not attributed on the route; the unrouted file of packet w02ca-p15-002 (lines 473-479) does so.

The unrouted files cross-reference one another (owned body lines 685-702 cite labels of the w02ca-p15-002 file, which in turn cites labels of the w02ca-p15-004 and w02ca-p15-008 files); they must be routed together for these references to resolve.
